title: Neuromorphic computing
outline: Lecture 18 video (Nature-Inspired Computation, ECM3412): Neuromorphic computing. 11 scenes, 126 s, built from videos/_plan/lecture-18-script.md. Running example: Priya's Hoglet, a battery hedgehog camera. Sources js/content/nic/l18-01.js (eventDemo seed 7, cameraDemo 12 x 6, unitsDemo seed 11 target 7.2, spikeFig, netFig), l18-02.js (18.1 to 18.3), l18-03.js (18.4 to 18.6), l18-workshop.js (18.W). ALL demo numbers are recomputed and asserted in videos/l18/common.js. COLOURS: orange = conventional side (von Neumann chip, clocked chip, frame camera); green = neuromorphic side (synapses, event-driven chip, event camera, best setting); purple = spikes; blue = data, memory, TrueNorth, deep learning; red = problems and costs; grey = neutral. Helpers: l5/common.js, l13/common*.js (tags, cards, stats, arrows) and l18/common-2.js (pictograms).

titleCard.title: Neuromorphic computing
titleCard.sub: Computers built like brains, that work only when a spike arrives

scenes.kicker: A COMPUTER SHAPED LIKE A BRAIN
title: Hoglet's chip
keeps making trips
caps: Hoglet watches the garden for hedgehogs all night.
Inside: a von Neumann computer, processor and memory apart.
A program runs step by step, in binary.
Data shuttles back and forth, and every trip costs energy.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 02-vonneumann: Hoglet, a hedgehog camera whose battery dies by Tuesday, holds an ordinary von Neumann computer: a processor (orange) and a separate memory (blue). A program runs step by step, in binary; data packets shuttle along the bus, faster and faster, each trip ticks a red counter and takes a sliver off the battery. Layout (stage px): left x 12..612: the garden (Hoglet on its post, a hedgehog, grass), later the 'inside Hoglet' panel with Processor (x 30..200) and Memory (x 420..590) boxes at y 330..450, the bus between them, the Program scroll above the processor. Right panel x 636..924: battery (y 24), 'dies by Tuesday' tag, 'trips' stat (y 250). Story (local seconds): 0.4 garden and Hoglet, 1.0 battery, 1.6 tag; 3.2 the garden fades, the panel and the two boxes pop; 6.0 the program scroll (step 1..3 light in turn) and the first packets; trips speed up to 11.6; 8.8 red label 'every trip costs time and energy'; hold to 12.

title: Synapses store
and compute
caps: In a neuromorphic computer, synapses store data and process it.
No program as such: the synapse structure sets what it does.
Inputs are spikes; their timing and magnitude carry information.
The term began in the 1980s; today it covers many brain-inspired ideas.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 03-neuromorphic: in a neuromorphic computer the synapses both store and compute (each green synapse carries a tiny memory cell); there is no program as such, the synapse structure sets what it does; inputs are spikes whose timing and magnitude carry information (lesson 18.1's spike trains, L18.RASTER); the term began in the 1980s. Layout (stage px): ghost von Neumann (grey Processor / Memory boxes, 'Program' tag) at x 12..232, y 12..250; the network (two inputs, two middle neurons, one output, six green synapses with memory cells) at x 300..880, y 30..230; structure tag at y 262; raster rows at y 380 / 450 / 520 (time 0..13 across x 200..876) with its tag at y 560; at 9.6 the raster fades and the 1980s -> today timeline takes its place (cards at y 360..540). Story (local seconds): 0.4 ghost, network neurons pop, synapses draw, memory cells pop; 3.2 'Program' fades, structure tag, a-c and d-e thicken, b-c thins; 6.0 a playhead sweeps the raster (6.2..8.2) and drops the purple spikes, 8.4 its tag; 9.6 the timeline (two cards and an arrow); hold to 13.

title: Parallel, collocated,
scalable
caps: Parallel: all neurons work at once, each doing something simple.
Processing and memory together: faster and less energy.
Scalable: need a bigger network? Add more chips.
And the fourth: it is event driven.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 04-superpowers: three of the four strengths of a neuromorphic chip, one row each (lesson 18.1): parallel, processing and memory collocated, scalable; a fourth empty slot announces 'event driven' (next scene). Layout (stage px): rows at y 12 / 168 / 324 / 480, 140 high. Each row: pictogram panel x 12..452, card x 468..924. Row 1: a 4 x 4 grid of green neurons that pulse together, beside one orange worker and a queue of 16 jobs lit one by one. Row 2: orange processor and blue memory boxes far apart with a blue packet running across the gap, beside two green neurons joined by a synapse with its memory cell (no gap). Row 3: chip tiles snap on one by one, joined by wires; a counter (times mark + number) shows 1..4. Row 4: a dashed slot with a doorbell and 'Event driven: next'. Story (local seconds): rows at 0.4 / 3.2 / 6.0 / 8.8 (panel, then card 0.3 s later), each animation starts with its row; chips snap at 6.4 / 6.9 / 7.4 / 7.9; hold to 12.

title: Clocked chip against
event-driven chip
caps: A quiet night: a spike at only 4 of 24 moments.
The clocked chip works 24 times; the event-driven chip 4.
A busier garden: 11 spikes, 11 bursts of work.
No spikes, no work: it computes only when a spike arrives.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 05-events: lesson 18.1's event demo (L18.NIGHT, seed 7, 24 moments). A playhead sweeps the night: purple spikes where something moved; the clocked chip (orange) works at every moment, the event-driven chip (green) only where a spike arrived. Activity 10 %: spikes at moments 5 8 9 23 (4 of 24); 50 %: 11; 0 %: none. Layout (stage px): row labels x 12..196; 24 cells across x 210..918 (pitch 29.5): spike row baseline y 100, clocked cells y 130..174, event cells y 206..250, moment labels '1' / '24' at y 258; activity slider y 330 (label, track x 210..918, knob, value, the label "activity" above the value); a doorbell at x 66, y 376 rings with each spike under the playhead; three stat tiles at y 420..570. Story (local seconds): 0.4 rows and tiles; sweep 0.6..3.1 at 10 %; 6.0 the slider glides to 50 %, rows clear, sweep 6.6..8.2; 8.8 the slider drops to 0 %, sweep 9.3..11.0 with no spikes, a 'silent' tag by the bell at 11.0; hold to 13.

title: Graphs, optimisation,
walkers and signals
caps: Graph algorithms: routing messages through a network.
Optimisation: constraint satisfaction, QUBO, optimal control.
Random walkers hop between neurons that stand for states.
Signal processing: steering vehicles, detecting seizures.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 06-jobs: what neuromorphic chips are good for (lesson 18.2), four quadrants filling in turn. Top left: graph algorithms, lesson 18.1's six-node network (L18.NET) with the route A B D E lighting blue hop by hop. Top right: optimisation, four tags (constraint satisfaction, QUBO, optimal control, Bayesian optimisation) and a note on LASSO. Bottom left: Markov chain random walkers, a hedgehog hops between four flower beds (each bed a neuron that spikes purple when the walker arrives; the hops come from L18.rng(5)). Bottom right: signal processing, a wave becomes purple spikes, then a green car and alarm bell: 'steer, or raise an alarm'. Layout (stage px): quadrants 450 x 306 at (12, 12), (474, 12), (12, 322), (474, 322), each a grey panel with a bold title. Story (local seconds): quadrants at 0.4 / 3.2 / 6.0 / 8.8; route hops at 1.2 + 0.5 i; optimisation tags 3.5 + 0.35 i, note 5.0; hops every 0.55 s from 6.6; signal: wave 9.1, spikes 9.7, icons 10.3, tag 10.8; hold to 12.

title: SpiNNaker, TrueNorth
and NorthPole
caps: SpiNNaker: 18 ARM cores per chip, built for exploring.
About 16,000 neurons in real time on 1 W per chip.
SpiNNaker 2, in 2019, is ten times bigger.
IBM TrueNorth: 1 million neurons per chip, set up in Corelet.
NorthPole, 2023: easier, faster, efficient AI.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 07-chips: the real machines of lesson 18.2 (facts from l18-02.js, L18.SPIN checks 1 + 17 = 18). Three cards, each a chip pictogram and stat lines that tick in. SpiNNaker (green): a chip with 18 core squares (6 x 3), one orange 'monitor' (runs the operating system), 17 green 'fascicle' cores (each models a group of neurons); lines 18 ARM cores, 128 MB shared, about 16,000 neurons, 8 million synapses, real time on 1 W; a tag 'SpiNNaker 2 (2019): ten times bigger'. TrueNorth (blue, IBM): 1 million neurons, 256 million synapses, programmed in Corelet. NorthPole (2023, green): usable in AI pipelines, low latency, efficient without losing accuracy. Layout (stage px): SpiNNaker card x 12..452, y 12..628: title, chip 150 px at (40, 80), legend right of it (x 216..440), stat lines from y 270, SpiNNaker 2 tag at y 532. TrueNorth card x 468..924, y 12..312; NorthPole card x 468..924, y 328..628: title, chip 110 px at the left, stat lines (28 px, may wrap) at x 620..910. Story (local seconds): 0.4 SpiNNaker card, cores pop 0.8..1.9, legend 2.0; lines 3.2 + 0.6 i; 6.6 the tag; 8.8 TrueNorth, lines 9.4 + 0.5 i; 11.2 NorthPole, lines 11.6 + 0.5 i; hold to 14.

scenes.kicker: SO WHY ISN'T HOGLET NEUROMORPHIC YET?
title: Promising,
but not there yet
caps: Deep learning still wins on results; neuromorphic wins on energy.
Little hardware and software to use, and long training times.
No benchmark suite that tests the time aspect.
Networks are wired neuron by neuron, which is error prone.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 08-whynot: why neuromorphic computing is not mainstream yet (lesson 18.3). Deep learning (blue) still wins on results, neuromorphic (green) wins on energy against edge GPUs; few machines, special-purpose simulators and long training (red strip); no shared benchmark that uses timing (a race track: the deep-learning lane has its ImageNet stopwatch, the neuromorphic lane has none); networks wired by hand, neuron by neuron (a cursor draws the nine arrows of a six-neuron network a, b -> c, d, e -> f), which is error prone, so examples lean on graph problems. Layout (stage px): top band y 12..200: Deep learning card x 12..300, Neuromorphic card x 636..924, middle x 312..624 two rows 'results' (y 40) and 'energy' (y 120) with a tick on the winning side. Red strip y 222 (three tags and arrows). Left half x 12..452, y 320..628: two race lanes and the red 'no shared benchmark' card. Right half x 468..924: the network (y 330..480) and two tags at y 500 / 562. Story (local seconds): 0.4 cards, 1.2 results row, 2.0 energy row; 3.2 strip tags 3.4 + 0.6 i; 6.0 lanes, 6.3 the stopwatch and ImageNet (it pulses at 7.8), 6.5 an empty dashed slot in the neuromorphic lane, 8.2 the red card; 9.4 neurons, arrows 9.8 + 0.2 i with the cursor, tags 11.6 / 12.0; hold.

scenes.kicker: A CAMERA THAT ONLY REPORTS CHANGE
title: Send only
what changed
caps: A frame camera sends all 72 pixels, every moment.
An event camera's pixels spike only when brightness changes: 2.
Hedgehog sits still: the event camera sends nothing.
Sensor fusion: wake the frame camera when events appear.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 09-camera: lesson 18.3's camera demo (L18.CAM): a 12 x 6 pixel garden, a hedgehog 2 pixels wide in row 4. The frame camera (orange) sends all 72 pixels every moment; the event camera (green) sends only the pixels whose brightness changed: 2 per moment while the hedgehog walks, none while it sits still. Totals: frame 216 / event 6 after three walking moments, frame 360 / event 6 after two still ones. Sensor fusion: events wake the frame camera for a photo. Layout (stage px): mode tag at y 12; grid x 12..612, y 70..370 (pitch 50, cells 46); note at y 386; right panel tiles x 636..924 at y 12 / 154 / 296 (130 high): Moments, Frame camera pixels sent, Event camera pixels sent; at 8.8 a flow strip at y 452 and a small photo frame at x 12..212, y 516..628. Story (local seconds): frame mode moments at 0.8 / 1.5 / 2.2 (all 72 pixels flash orange); 3.2 event mode, fresh count, the hedgehog starts again: moments 3.6 / 4.3 / 5.0 (the 2 changed pixels flash green); 6.0 the hedgehog sits still: moments 6.4 / 7.1, frame adds 72 each, event nothing, 7.3 the note; 8.8 the strip tags 9.0 + 0.5 i, the photo 10.4; hold to 12.

title: Spike, jump;
no spike, step
caps: GAs and PSO are parallel but energy hungry on normal hardware.
Neuromorphic heuristic units evolve candidates asynchronously.
No spike: a heuristic step, towards the best so far.
A spike: the neuron's own dynamics make a jump.
Promising, but still highly experimental.
scenes.spec: Lecture 18 video, scene 10-units: lesson 18.3's spiking heuristic units (L18.UNITS, unitsDemo seed 11, a toy). GAs and PSO are parallel but energy hungry on ordinary hardware. Five units U1..U5 each hold a candidate setting (0..10) and a charge; a manager and selector coordinate. No spike: a heuristic step towards the best so far (7.2). Spike: the neuron's own dynamics make a jump. U1: 2.8 -> 5.2 -> 6.3 -> spike 1.3 -> 4.0. Layout (stage px): header y 12..100 (GA and PSO chips, a draining battery, 'parallel, but energy hungry'), replaced at 9.8 by the orange banner; manager card y 118..172 (from 6.0 the move legend instead); five lanes at y 190 + 76 i (h 70): 'U1'.. at x 12, axis x 100..760 (0..10), charge bar x 790..924; the green 'best 7.2' line at x 575 with its label at y 586. Story (local seconds): 0.4 header, battery drains 0.8..2.8; 3.2 manager, lanes 3.4 + 0.15 i, the best line 4.0; the lanes pulse out of step from 4.2; 6.0 the other lanes fade, U1 ticks at 6.3 / 7.0 (steps, grey arrows), 8.2 (spike: charge full, purple flash and arrow), 9.0 (step); 9.8 the banner; hold to 12.

recap.spec: Lecture 18 · Neuromorphic computing, scene 11-recap: three rows, each a small animated pictogram and one bold line (bare scene). Story (local seconds): 0.1 title and Sprout, rows slide in at 0.8 / 1.9 / 3.0, each pictogram starts 0.4 s after its row, 4.2-4.8 the call to action 'Next: Workshop 18.W'. EVERY PICTOGRAM PLAYS ONCE AND HOLDS ITS FINISHED FRAME (no loop, no reset): all are done by 6.5 s, so for the rest only Sprout's bob moves. Row 1 (green): two neurons joined by a synapse; the synapse draws, then its memory cell pops on it (no separate memory). Row 2 (purple): a row of eight grey cells; two purple spikes drop and only the two cells under them light green. Row 3 (orange): a battery fills and stays nearly full, a flask pops in beside it (still experimental).
